schemaNotes: Single source of truth for account-deletion data classification. Every user-keyed write destination across src/ and functions/ must appear here in either included[] or excluded[]. The drift-prevention test (src/lib/__tests__/accountDeletionDrift.test.ts) scans the codebase and fails if any detected user-keyed write is unclassified. New collections require a new entry here before the test passes. CI must mark the drift test as a required check.

domains.A_private: Private user-owned data (food diary, training, weight, etc.)
domains.D_crossUserEdge: Edges/references involving the user (follows, blocks, memberships)
domains.E_fanout: Fan-out / denormalised copies in other users' trees
domains.H_excluded: Retained or anonymised — see reason on each entry
domains.Z_operational: Records written by the deletion subsystem itself (ledger, tombstone, post-deletion payment log)

strategies.deleteSubcollection: Iterate the subcollection in batches and delete every doc
strategies.deleteQueryInBatches: Run a where() query and batch-delete results until empty
strategies.deleteCollectionGroupInBatches: collectionGroup() across the project, filtered by stored uid field, batch-delete
strategies.anonymise: Update doc to clear user-identifying fields (authorId, displayName, photoURL); preserve thread/audit content

lockTypes.direct-rules: Firestore rules deny client writes while accountDeletionRequests/{uid}.status is active
lockTypes.callable-actor: Cloud Function callable rejects writes when context.auth.uid has active deletion
lockTypes.referenced-uid: Cloud Function callable creating cross-user references rejects when any referenced uid has active deletion (transactional check)
lockTypes.system-writer: Background/scheduled/webhook function checks deletedAccounts tombstone before recreating user data
lockTypes.none: No lock needed (e.g. read-only, write happens during deletion itself)

included.reason: User food diary — meal-by-meal log with descriptions, macros, photo refs, timestamps
Lifting workout log — exercise sets, reps, weight, RPE, dates
Run log — GPS tracks (privacy-zoned), pace splits, durations, dates
Bodyweight history — datapoints. Legacy aliases catch pre-rename docs from earlier app versions
Daily hydration log — per-day water intake records
Saved foods — names, macros, serving sizes user has favourited for quick-add
Running shoe inventory — names, mileage, retirement dates
GPS coordinates of home/work — explicitly precise location data, must not persist after deletion
User-configured reminders, notification prefs, display options
Personal record map — best lifts, fastest splits, derived from workouts
Active workout program plan — current phase, scheduled sessions, progression state
User-authored workout routines — exercise lists, naming, organisation
Diagnostic error reports including stack traces, may contain user-context fields like meal text or food names from the surface where the error occurred
Daily roll-up logs — per-day summary docs derived from meals/workouts/runs
Streak state and badge earn dates — derived from activity history
Firestore docs referencing progress photo blobs in Storage. Storage blob cleanup is separate (progressPhotosStorage)

Weekly performance index rollups — written by scheduled functions, derived from workouts and runs. Lock type is system-writer (deleteMyAccount sweep happens server-side; rules already deny client writes per firestore.rules:116-119)
Performance engine concurrency lock doc — written by performance rollup functions to serialise weekly recompute. No PII but tied to user account
Cross-user-readable public projection — displayName, photoURL, badgeSummary, currentStreak. Must delete BEFORE users/{uid} root since rules read it

Root user doc — profile, onboarding state, subscription fields (stripeCustomerId / appleOriginalTransactionId), preferences. Must delete LAST after all subcollections (and after public/profile) since deleting the parent before children would leave orphans accessible via collectionGroup queries
User's own home feed — denormalised copies of activities they follow. Cleaned together with fan-out (feedFanout) but distinct path
Notifications addressed to the user (kudos received, comments on user's posts, follow events)
List of users this account follows. Mirror in followers/{otherUid}/users/{uid} cleaned via followingMirror
List of users who follow this account. Mirror in following/{otherUid}/users/{uid} cleaned via followersMirror
Users this account has blocked. Reverse-direction blocks (others blocking this user) cleaned via blocksReverse
Monthly AI food-scan quota counter. Server-only writes (functions/index.js:191). No PII but user-keyed; deleting closes the audit loop
Per-action rate-limit counters keyed {uid}_{action}. Server-only writes (functions/index.js:128-150). Detected via doc-id prefix match
Public activities authored by the user (workout/run/PR posts). Already covered today via authorId query — ported to inventory

Fan-out copies of this user's posts denormalised into other users' feed subcollections. CollectionGroup query filtered by authorId. pathFilter must constrain to feeds/* parents only — generic 'items' collectionGroup blast radius would also match comments/{*}/items and trigger comment deletion which is handled separately by anonymisation
Notifications this user generated for others (kudos given, comments made, follow notifications). Same pathFilter discipline as feedFanout
For each follow this user made, delete the mirror in the target's followers list. Iterate following/{uid}/users BEFORE deleting that subcollection so we have the targetUid list
For each follower of this user, delete the mirror in the follower's following list. Iterate followers/{uid}/users BEFORE deleting it

Other users who blocked this account — doc id equals deleted user's uid. Low harm but tidies references. Filter required: collectionGroup('users') is overly broad without pathFilter (it would also match following/{uid}/users and followers/{uid}/users)

Crew/group memberships keyed by uid as doc id, with denormalised displayName. Must also decrement memberCount on the parent group doc in a transaction — leaving stale counts breaks crew leaderboard rendering
Challenge participations keyed by uid as doc id with denormalised progress. Decrement participantCount on parent challenge in a transaction

Kudos this user gave on others' activities — doc id equals uid. CollectionGroup('users') needs pathFilter to avoid matching following/followers/blocks subcollections (same name). Decrement kudosCount on each affected activity. Existing docs lack a userId field; cleanup must rely on doc-id-equals filter (Firestore supports __name__ collectionGroup filters since 2023)
Avatar/profile photos. Storage rules write-freeze via custom auth claim (storage.rules cannot read Firestore directly)
Progress photo blobs (encrypted webp). Storage rules write-freeze via custom auth claim

excluded.reason: Comments this user posted on other users' activities. Anonymising rather than deleting preserves thread context for the activity owner and other commenters; deleting would leave reply chains broken. Removing authorId/displayName/photoURL severs the PII linkage to the deleted account

Moderation reports filed BY OTHERS about this user. Operationally needed for safety/legal review even after the account is deleted — abuse history about a deleted account stays in the moderation log so future re-registrations under same email can be flagged
Reports this user filed against others. Retain the report content (reason, targetId) for moderation continuity; anonymise reporterId to remove the deleted user's identity from the trail

excluded.minimisationRule: Only fields permitted: provider (apple|stripe), externalTxnId, eventType, occurredAt, hashedUidPrefix (first 8 chars of SHA256(uid)), action ('skipped'|'logged'). NO email, displayName, profile photo URLs, full receipt payloads, transaction amounts, or any user-identifying fields beyond the externalTxnId issued by the provider
excluded.reason: Created by Apple/Stripe webhooks when a payment event arrives for a uid in the deletedAccounts tombstone. Operator-reviewable log so genuine billing issues (e.g. refund obligations) are visible without leaking PII. Written by webhook system writers, never by client

excluded.minimisationRule: Only fields permitted from accountDeletionLedger.SCHEMA. Forbidden: meal names, workout notes, route coords, photos, comment bodies, displayName, email, photoURL, receipt payloads. Operational record only
excluded.reason: Operational ledger tracking deletion lease, status transitions, leaseGeneration fencing. Required by spec Phase 2. Bounded retention via Firestore TTL on cleanupAfter field — founder must enable TTL policy after deploy

excluded.minimisationRule: Only fields permitted: uid, deletedAt, source, billingRetention. Forbidden: any profile/content data. Personal-data flag is true because uid alone is a personal identifier per GDPR
excluded.reason: Long-term tombstone covering the gap after accountDeletionLedger TTL expires. System writers (Apple/Stripe webhooks, Firestore triggers) check this before recreating user data. 90d window covers monthly billing cycle + Apple receipt re-verification + late webhook retries. Indefinite retention would itself be a compliance issue (uid is PII), so bounded decay is the trade-off
